title: Separating Mixtures
seo_title: Year 5 Science: Separating Mixtures Worksheets (Sieving, Filtering, Evaporating)
standard_code: Year 5: Properties and changes of materials
standard_text: Use knowledge of solids, liquids and gases to decide how mixtures might be separated, including through filtering, sieving and evaporating.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 science worksheets on separating mixtures: sieving, filtering, evaporating and magnets, separating a mixture in steps, and recovering materials. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Pick the method that fits the materials.
key_sub: Sieve sizes, filter insoluble bits, evaporate dissolved ones, use a magnet for iron.
body_html:
How to think about it

Choose a separating method using the properties of the materials.

  • Sieving: solids with different-sized pieces. Magnet: magnetic metals (iron, steel).
  • Filtering: an insoluble solid from a liquid (sand from water). Evaporating: a dissolved solid from a liquid (salt from water).
  • For sand, salt and iron: magnet → add water and stir → filter → evaporate.
Example

Salt and water?

Salt is dissolved

Answer: evaporate the water

Example

Gravel and sand?

Different-sized pieces

Answer: sieve

Common mistakes

  • Thinking filtering removes dissolved salt.
  • Thinking a magnet picks up all metals.
  • Thinking evaporating destroys the salt.

faq.q: How do you separate sand from water?
faq.a: Filter it. The insoluble sand is caught by the filter paper and the water passes through.

faq.q: How do you get salt back from salt water?
faq.a: Evaporate the water by heating it or leaving it in a warm place. The salt is left behind.

faq.q: How would you separate sand, salt and iron filings?
faq.a: Use a magnet to take out the iron, add water and stir to dissolve the salt, filter out the sand, then evaporate the water to get the salt.
